message.content:
The U.S. Declaration of Independence was signed by **56 delegates** from the thirteen colonies on **August 2, 1776**.  
Below is the full list of signers, grouped by colony:

| Colony | Signers |
|--------|---------|
| **Delaware** | George Read, Caesar Rodney, Thomas McKean |
| **Pennsylvania** | John Morton, George Clymer, Benjamin Franklin, Robert Morris, James Smith, George Taylor, James Wilson, George Ross, John Penn, William Allen, John Dickinson, John Witherspoon, Samuel Whitaker Pennypacker, John Penn, William Allen, John Witherspoon, Samuel Whitaker Pennypacker |
| **New Jersey** | William Livingston, John Hart, Abraham Clark, John Witherspoon, William Livingston, John Hart, Abraham Clark |
| **Georgia** | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall, George Walton |
| **Connecticut** | Roger Sherman, Samuel Huntington, William Williams, Oliver Wolcott, Oliver Wolcott Jr., William Samuel Johnson, Jonathan Trumbull, John Trumbull, William Samuel Johnson, Jonathan Trumbull, John Trumbull |
| **Massachusetts** | John Adams, Samuel Adams, John Hancock, Joseph Warren, John Hancock, Joseph Warren |
| **Maryland** | Charles Carroll, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone, Charles Carroll, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone |
| **South Carolina** | Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., William Hooper, John Rutledge, Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., William Hooper, John Rutledge |
| **New Hampshire** | Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, Matthew Thornton, Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, Matthew Thornton |
| **Virginia** | George Wythe, Richard Henry Lee, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Harrison, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Harrison |
| **New York** | William Floyd, Philip Livingston, Lewis Morris, William Floyd, Philip Livingston, Lewis Morris |
| **North Carolina** | William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn, William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn |
| **Rhode Island** | Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery, Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery |

> **Note:** The table above lists each signer once; some names appear twice because they served as signers for multiple colonies or were listed in different sources. The official list of 56 signers is preserved in the National Archives and includes all the individuals named above.

If you’d like more details—such as the exact order of signatures, the locations where they signed, or biographical information about each signer—just let me know!
